questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z)\text{ }k \\  & =(1-2xz)\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j-{x}^{2}k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,2) & =(\,1-2(1)(2)\,)\text{ }i+2(1)\text{ }j-(1)^{2}k \\  & =-3\,i+2\,j-1\,k \\  & =⟨-3,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-3,2,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface ${x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}=17.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,-2,1),$ what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=17.$   

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(2,-2,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1})j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}))k \\  & =2x{y}^{2}i+2y{x}^{2}j+{e}^{z-1}k \\ ∇f(2,-2,1) & =2(2)(-2)^{2}\text{ }i+2(-2){2}^{2}\text{ }j+{e}^{1-1}\text{ }k \\  & =16\text{ }i-16\text{ }j+\text{ }k \\  & =⟨16,\,-16,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨16,\,-16,\,1⟩.$ 

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{16}{1}=16.$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $\operatorname{ln}⁡{(xy+yz+1)}^{3}=3\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,1),$ what is the value of $\frac{a+b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy+yz+1).$ Then, since $\operatorname{ln}⁡{(xy+yz+1)}^{3}=3\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy+yz+1)$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).$    

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy+yz+1))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy+yz+1))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy+yz+1))k \\  & =(\frac{1}{xy+yz+1}\cdot y)i+(\frac{1}{xy+yz+1}\cdot (x+z))j+(\frac{1}{xy+yz+1}\cdot y)k \\  & =\frac{y}{xy+yz+1}\text{ }i+\frac{x+z}{xy+yz+1}\text{ }j+\frac{y}{xy+yz+1}\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,1,1) & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 1+1\cdot 1+1}\text{ }i+\frac{1+1}{1\cdot 1+1\cdot 1+1}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{1\cdot 1+1\cdot 1+1}\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\text{ }i+\frac{2}{3}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{3}\text{ }k \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3}⟩.$ 

Finally, $\frac{a+b}{c}=\frac{(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{3})}{(\frac{1}{3})}=3.$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }k \\  & =2y{e}^{x}\text{ }i+2{e}^{x}\text{ }j-{e}^{z}k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,-1) & =2(1)e\text{ }i+2e\text{ }j-{e}^{-1}k \\  & =2e\,i+2e\,j-{e}^{-1}k \\  & =⟨2e,2e,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2e,2e,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ 2ex+2ey-\frac{z}{e}-4e-\frac{1}{e} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3})\text{ }k \\  & =({z}^{3}-y)\text{ }i+(3z{y}^{2}-x)\text{ }j+(3x{z}^{2}+{y}^{3})k \\ ∇\,f(2,-1,1) & =({1}^{3}-(-1))\text{ }i+(3(1)(-1)^{2}-2)\text{ }j+(3(2)(1)^{2}+(-1)^{3})k \\  & =2\,i+\,j+5k \\  & =⟨2,1,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,1,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$
